correctness.rationale: The coefficient identity reduces the sextic to abc+2(a+b+c)^3 for a=x²,b=y²,c=z². The quotient cubic has only the full-support node; a reduced reducible cubic would force a second intersection or a nonordinary singularity by Bézout, and a repeated component is excluded by the finite singular support. On its normalization a/c and b/c have valuation pairs (3,0) and (0,3) at two distinct smooth axis points, so their square classes are independent. The torus pullback is a field generically and étale there, with no component on an axis. The derivatives exhaust support: four full-support nodes (tangent discriminant 3) and six axis cusps (independent local parameters xy and x²+y²+1 in the z=1 chart, equation U²+2V³). The local Jacobian lengths are 1 and 2. Total delta 10 gives genus zero and a rational cusp lifts to a rational point. At odd degrees each nonsplit node adds one relative to normalization, at even degrees each subtracts one; the cusps contribute zero. This proves the sign, exponent and universal formula, not just two finite counts.
residual_risks: The frozen script checks two extension fields; the review establishes the all-extension statement by the geometric argument, not a rerun of that script.
